extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, IPRA members, prospective members, and PR industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A historical summary of the International Public Relations Association (IPRA) that also documents its ethical codes, governance, awards and judging standards used to recognise excellence in public relations practice worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding objective: raising PR standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise public relations professionals into a transnational society with the objective of raising standards of public relations practice in the various countries and improving the quality and efficiency of practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This foundational objective motivated IPRA’s formation and underpins its activities: promoting exchange of information, cooperation across countries, and initiatives aimed at enhancing PR's role in management and international affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings and World Public Relations Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRA Council and Board meet regularly (normally with national PR association conferences) and every three years IPRA sponsors a World Public Relations Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These meetings are used to review organisational activities, focus membership on emerging PR issues, assess latest standards and techniques of practice, and explore means of increasing cooperation internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPRA Code of Conduct (1961)
rubrics_metrics.description: An IPRA Code of Conduct adopted to establish accepted standards of professional ethics and behaviour to be adhered to by all members worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to highlight ethical, moral and socially responsible aspects of the profession; served as an inspiration and basis for similar national PR association codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Ethics — 'Code of Athens' (1965)
rubrics_metrics.description: An International Code of Ethics (informally the 'Code of Athens') approved by IPRA, constituting the Association’s moral charter and inspired by the United Nations Declaration of Human Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authored by Lucien Matrat, promoted widely (presented to Heads of State). In 2011 the various IPRA codes were consolidated into a single updated document to reflect contemporary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPRA consultative status with UN bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRA is recognised as an international non-governmental organisation by the United Nations system and has been granted consultative status by ECOSOC and by UNESCO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognition underlines IPRA’s role in international relations and its authority in advising on PR-related international policy and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPRA President’s Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Award established (1977) to celebrate 'outstanding contributions to better world understanding.' Recipients include individuals or institutions which have utilised the tools of mass communication to promote the principles of peace, social justice, cultural understanding or the role of public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of recipients: Nobel Foundation, International Red Cross, Band Aid, WWF, Archbishop Desmond Tutu. The prize recognises use of mass communication to advance those social goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golden World Awards (GWA) judging standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Relations programmes submitted to the Golden World Awards are judged according to the quality of their research, planning, execution and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than one award can be given in each category. An overall Grand Prix for Excellence is presented to the entry judged as most representing the highest standards of PR practice. Trophies are presented to award recipients. Sponsorship history is noted but not a judging factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Contribution Award / alignment with UN SDGs
rubrics_metrics.description: What is now called the Global Contribution Award recognises programmes that meet one of the 17 United Nations sustainable development goals (SDGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award explicitly links judged programme impact to one of the UN SDGs as a criterion of global contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to professional development (especially in emerging PR markets)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPRA places special emphasis on professional development in countries where PR is emerging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include building programmes of professional development opportunities and initiatives aimed at enhancing the role of public relations in management and international affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance structure and member representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2011, IPRA's Board and Council have been merged and members elect the Board based on geographic region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural adaptation reflects the organisation’s international representation and strategic planning needs; it is a governance requirement affecting how IPRA operates and represents members.
